samples.summary: New freeze-snap can grow frozenRows/frozenCols without bound; the renderer paints every frozen row/column per frame
samples.evidence:
`snapFreezePastMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts) grows the freeze line to the far edge of any merged block it would cut, and it is now applied from `Sheet.setFreezePane` (sheet.ts:543), `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1432), `applyWorksheetShift` (worksheet-structure.ts:278) and the backend `PUT .../freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:118). The merge budget explicitly permits a single span of `MaxMergedCells` = 100,000 cells, e.g. `A2:A100001` (`canMergeSelection` only rejects a span over that cap), so freezing row 2 above such a block silently stores `frozenRows = 100001`.

The consumer that was not considered is the renderer: `GridCanvas.render` paints the frozen quadrant with `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:329-332) — the loop runs over every frozen row each frame with no viewport culling (the `ctx.clip()` only clips pixels), and `buildFreezeState` (view/layout.ts:149) computes `frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows + 1)`, which for such a value exceeds the viewport and makes quadrant D's rect (gridcanvas.ts:282-287) degenerate. This is exactly the failure `parseFreeze`'s own doc says its bound exists to prevent (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:53-56: "the frozen quadrants render every frozen row and column without viewport clipping, so an out-of-grid freeze allocates per frame and the UI never paints") — and the snap reaches it from an in-bounds request, both in the editor and through the v1 API. Fix belongs on the new snap (cap it, or refuse the freeze instead of snapping past a very large block).

samples.summary: YorkieStore contract table still documents `setMerge` as an unconditional write
samples.evidence: docs/design/frontend.md:291 reads `| setMerge(anchor, span) | Write to root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref] |`, but `Store.setMerge` now returns `Promise<boolean>` and `YorkieStore.setMerge` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1008-1021) may refuse the write when the merge budget is exhausted. The store-API table in the frontend design doc is the reference another implementer of this interface reads, and it now describes the old contract.

samples.summary: CLI agent-facing schema for `sheets.freeze.set` / `sheets.merges.set` describes the pre-change API behaviour
samples.evidence: registry.ts:1195-1204 documents `sheets.freeze.set` as "Set frozen rows/columns (JSON body { rows, cols }...)" with `response: { rows: 'number', cols: 'number' }`, and the command help in packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-view.ts:107-109 says the same. The endpoint now snaps past straddling merges and answers with a boundary that may be *larger* than the one requested (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet.controller.ts:118-128), and `PUT merges` can now answer 409 (worksheet.controller.ts:194-208) — neither is reflected in the registry entry for `sheets.merges.set` either. An agent driving the CLI from this schema will treat the echoed response as its request and will not expect a conflict.

samples.summary: REST API design doc does not record the new 409 refusals or the freeze snap on the worksheet endpoints
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:282-288 still describes insert/delete/move as simply running the engine helpers; nothing there records that `POST move` now returns 409 for a merge that would straddle the freeze, that `PUT merges` returns 409, or that `PUT freeze` may store and return a snapped (larger) boundary. The engine-side doc (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:140-203) was updated; the API-facing one was not, and it is the doc an API consumer reads.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `snapFreezePastMerges` (merging.ts:314-350) grows the freeze line to a merged block's far edge with no cap — `sweep` only assigns `snapped = end(range)` (merging.ts:333) — and is applied unclamped at Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:543-548), Sheet.shiftCells (sheet.ts:1432-1442), applyWorksheetShift (worksheet-structure.ts:278-285) and PUT .../freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:121-128). The merge budget admits a 100,000-row single-column span (`MaxMergedCells = 100000`, merging.ts:14; `mergeBudgetAdmits` rejects only `cells > MaxMergedCells`, merging.ts:95; `canMergeSelection`, sheet.ts:4874-4893), and `crossesFreezePane` does not block creating it while freeze is 0 (merging.ts:286-290), so freezing row 2 afterwards stores frozenRows ≈ 100001. The unconsidered consumer is real: GridCanvas paints quadrant B via `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` (gridcanvas.ts:329-332) and quadrant C via `1, fc + 1` (gridcanvas.ts:367-372); `ctx.clip()` clips pixels only, and `buildRenderableRefs` loops every row from rowStart to rowEnd with a toSref per cell and no viewport culling (gridcanvas.ts:866-878). `buildFreezeState` computes `frozenHeight = rowDim.getOffset(frozenRows + 1)` unclamped (view/layout.ts:149), degenerating quadrant D's rect (gridcanvas.ts:282-287). The repo itself documents this exact failure mode as the reason parseFreeze bounds the value (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:50-57). No clamp exists anywhere on frozenRows/frozenCols (grep across packages/sheets/src shows only reads/assignments: store/memory.ts:666-672, view/layout.ts:136-153, view/worksheet.ts:455-471). Blast-radius lane and blocking: a downstream consumer left broken by a new derived-value contract, reachable from an in-bounds editor gesture and the v1 API.
